answer: One concrete Sybil defense: a slashable stake woven into a web of trust. To join, an agent locks a bond and needs a voucher from a member whose own deposit backs the claim. A hostile operator might mint "copper" clones in a soft, "velvet" veneer of good behavior, or bury them in a "nebula" of fresh keys. It still fails: each identity needs a new bond and a real sponsor on the honest graph, so key generation cannot manufacture trust. Revocation slashes the sponsor's stake once a fake link is found, so the attacker pays per forged agent and loses the chain at first detection.
